reader_identity: /root/blind_b; independent image-only second reader for scan033
independence_statement: I read only the assigned CONVENTIONS.md and scan033 boxes TSV as textual inputs, then the assigned whole source JPG and my independently generated crops. I did not open witnesses, page.tex, first-reader transcriptions or crops, notes, review records, another reader's output, or any script containing pre-existing readings. I used no OCR, recognition library, external research or TeX compilation. Every listed box was personally visually inspected. The readings and uncertainties were formed before any comparison with another reader.
crop_processing: Pillow crop in original coordinates; rotation 0 except the two marginal crops at -90 degrees (clockwise); autocontrast cutoff 0.5; LANCZOS enlargement to 3000 px across; UnsharpMask radius 1.2, percent 110, threshold 3. No strokes removed or added.

boxes.observations: Two separate clear numerals: open upper/lower lobes of 3, then curved top and long right foot of 2. A single dense terminal dot follows. No crossing-out.

A compact overwritten initial glyph has a left stem and loop/diagonal remnants; R or F cannot be separated securely. To its right a right-pointing arrow has two shaft traces. The ordinal has a vertical stem, small raised circle and closing parenthesis; the two set-difference obliques and both primes are visible. The relation is an open c-shaped subset sign.

The target between donc and the opening parenthesis contains an A-shaped triangle and a small membership-like curve crossed by an additional diagonal and heavy basal stroke. I retained deletion and uncertainty. Parenthetic comme, G with hooked right end, a two-stroke less/equal relation, and final A membership G are readable.

The first mark has a 2-shaped descending curve and looped base, a raised small circle, then a parenthesis. F-prime and G-prime each carry a distinct short upper stroke. Both set-difference strokes and the open subset sign are separate. Soit reaches the right edge; later context is not included.

A-prime, membership and F are intact, followed by a full stop. A tall loop at the beginning of the cancelled phrase and low connected residual strokes suggest On a; a heavy horizontal line runs through the phrase. Soit and A are intact. The following le is clipped by the right edge and is omitted.

The A-prime following F is raised above its baseline, so I read a superscript. Below the two right-hand formulas is one continuous thin underline/bracket with upturned ends. The first relation is heavily retraced, with a lower extra loop; subset versus subset-or-equal is uncertain. The superscript after the next A is a small loop with a descending right stroke, provisionally varphi or q. In the second expression A-prime is followed by a small round superscript and (F-prime). The final exponent hits the physical right edge of the whole source after an F-like glyph; I did not supply the unseen closing parenthesis or a prime.

Between the two As are two thick horizontal strokes plus a surviving left connector and short internal stroke; I cannot decide whether the final retracing means equals or membership. The parenthetic word has d-loop, apostrophe and reduced trailing strokes, provisionally d'où. The second A has no separately identifiable prime. A terminal On a-like phrase is horizontally struck. Detail revisited the relation and parenthetic phrase.

Clockwise rotation makes the vertical writing upright. The beginning reads on a; the long middle word has an i-dot, a low m-like stretch and tall p/l/f strokes, suggesting simplifié but reduced ending remains doubtful. A comma separates cf, whose f descends across the long rule. plus is readable. The final abbreviated tall letter can be b or h; I have not expanded it to bas or haut. The line beside the note is thin and continuous, without an arrowhead.

Cancelled word begins with a clear two-stem M, then an a-loop and i-dot; terminal strokes are covered by the cancellation, so Mais remains qualified. A dense horizontal strike traverses it. Donc to the right has an unstruck capital D and low nc strokes.

After the preceding comma is a small crossed group with an e-like lower loop and a tall t-like stroke/crossbar. Multiple obliques obscure the letters, retained as doubtful et. To its right the next capital/lowercase pair reads Il. Partial neighbouring F-prime and en are not promoted to target text.

Both main letters are A. On each is a small raised round o/circle and parenthetic F; only the right F carries a distinct prime. The equality has two short horizontal strokes. Parentheses belong to the exponents; the right closing parenthesis is large but present.

The interlinear phrase has i-dot/l-stem, then s and two tall f strokes with reduced it ending. F-prime is followed by two distinct left-angle strokes and then F. A thin curved attachment line runs below the addition and bends up at its right end, separating it from the baseline text.

The baseline starts with an opening parenthesis and car, then an intact F-prime. The less/equal-shaped sign is very heavily retraced and crossed near its upper arm; F has an abnormal horizontal bar extending across its centre. I retain uncertainty over their cancellation state. A separate loop/right-parenthesis-like mark is crossed at the insertion attachment. cf is complete; the following lemme extends into the right crop edge and is omitted from this excerpt.

After a closing parenthesis, et is joined in a looped cursive form. The next word has a tall b-loop, i-dot and a low terminal n, read bien. A distinct short line lies below the middle of bien; whether deliberate underlining or a pen return is retained as state uncertainty. There is no full crossing stroke through the word.

The leading cancelled sign has a vertical/spine and horizontal fragments, more E-like than a secure quantifier; two diagonals cross it. A comma separates A and A-prime, then membership F-prime and tels que. The left exponent includes A-prime, circle and (F-prime); the right is unprimed A with circle and (F-prime). The relation is a small open subset sign. The final ce qui/ce que is reduced and remains uncertain.

Donc has a clear capital D; on a is very lightly written but separate from the following p-descender of prouvé, which ends with an accent stroke. The A before membership is retraced with an extra outer curve, but the final triangular A and prime are legible; no separate deleted original letter can be recovered.

Opening parenthesis, d'où and A-prime membership F difference G are visible. Between G and the following cqd-like abbreviation is a tall looped mark with crossed upper arms and two descending curves; I provisionally treat it as a cancelled closing parenthesis. The last d has a tall loop and the final closing parenthesis and dot are clear. I retained the source parenthesis state, including the cancelled one.

Initial S-like loop, i/apostrophe-like mark and compressed low strokes do not securely distinguish Sinon from Si; a distinct following on-shaped low group is present. In the next word the final ait, including i-dot and tall t, is clear, while the middle v/u-r strokes are reduced. I retain avait/aurait uncertainty. A-prime membership G and comma are clear.

Small interlinear text begins with looped On and suppose-like strokes, followed by b), i.e., a phi-like letter and an induit-like word. Both ends of the arrow were inspected: F-prime difference G-prime on the left, F difference G on the right; a wavy tilde is above a right-pointing arrow. The thin curved attachment line goes below the insertion. Long diagonal block-cancellation strokes also pass through this line, so the insertion is enclosed in deletion.

The b) and c) flank a two-shaft right arrow. Soit, A membership F difference G, and prouvons que are readable. Several long diagonal strokes run through the line and continue across the following lines; this excerpt retains the enclosing deletion.

The phrase starts with compressed str.-like strokes and a small tall t-like suffix, then a separated dash and ouvert. pour has a descender crossing the thin underline. A compact cancelled capital before the surviving F-prime is obscured by multiple horizontal/diagonal strokes, provisionally F or A. One continuous underline runs below the phrase and stops before the surviving F-prime. Long diagonal block cancellations cross this entire passage.

The target has the tall l and accented/e-like groups of élément, followed by a small loop and low horizontal stroke where de is separately struck. tel que follows with a high t and descender of q. The larger diagonal block strikes and underline from the preceding line are visible; I preserve both the enclosing cancellation and the smaller de deletion.

Prouvons is visible below the heavily crossed preceding line. The left A has a prime, small round superscript and (F-prime); the right A has the round superscript and (F) without a prime. Equality is two dark parallel strokes, followed by a dense full stop. Although this bottom line is less directly crossed, its attachment to the cancelled proof is clear in the larger block crop, so the enclosing deletion is retained.

b and c flank a double-headed two-shaft arrow. Posons has a clear initial P and o but is centrally crossed; uncertainty retained. On a follows separately. Vertical bars enclose each F and G; the difference signs are oblique strokes between the barred expressions. Only the right F and G are primed. The last word is soit and the symbol is a squared U followed by comma.

F difference G equals a serifed I with a small raised k/left-arrow-like mark; the same small mark recurs after I-prime on the right. Each has a short rightward stroke and a left upright/angled component; I have not silently normalized these to stars. Between F-prime and G-prime is a compact, heavily crossed diagonal group: a cancelled difference mark is the preferred state, with an intact retraced difference as alternative. A detail crop was independently examined.

The text reads des ens d'indices ordonnés, with ens left abbreviated and no securely separate stop. The serifed I has a rightward arrow drawn along/above its top bar. After a comma is a separately cancelled angular capital, provisionally A or F. The parenthesis contains equals and a looped F/P-like letter. Partial upper and lower lines are excluded.

Serifed I bears a clear prime. Parenthesis encloses an equals sign and F-prime; a distinct dot follows the closing parenthesis. On is looped and the following a is very reduced to a dark small form, matching its place on the baseline. I read On a, not a separate terminal punctuation dot.

Close inspection shows the first A-prime, a dense open curved relation, then A with a raised loop-and-descender mark. The relation has a separate-looking lower trace but no clean isolated equality bar, so subset is preferred over subset-or-equal. The superscript resembles varphi or q. The continuous underline/bracket under this excerpt is clear and continues beyond the box.

The enlarged leading sign shows a left stem/spine, an upper horizontal arm, a shorter middle bar, a curved lower tail, and two strong crossing diagonals. E is a visual candidate; a damaged universal quantifier is another. I do not replace it with a textual illegibility macro. The following A comma A-prime are clear.

The two-line crop supplies both sides of the implication: A-prime membership F-prime difference G-prime above, then the right arrow and A-prime membership F below. The first A is overwritten but legible in its final state. Prouvons qu'on a follows, and the final membership sign has a clear vertical oblique crossing to form not-in before G. No initial prime was supplied to the unprimed F in the consequent.

The whole block shows five long diagonal cancellation strokes across the b-to-c proof and its small upper insertion. The insertion is attached by a thin curved line under its words. A-circ(F) is followed by est un and a separately underlined abbreviated -ouvert phrase; a capital before F-prime is locally struck. Next line has A-prime membership F-prime difference G-prime, l'unique élément, a locally crossed de, and phi(A-prime)=A. The final Prouvons equality belongs to the same block. I retain the outer deletion, inner deletion, insertion and underline as distinct states.

The I at left has a right-pointing arrow on its top bar. A comma precedes an angular glyph struck by an ascending diagonal and dense horizontal crossing; A or F are tentative. The next parenthesis is intact with an equals sign and a capital whose top forms a rounded loop with a short lower horizontal, suggesting F with P as alternative. boxes.observations: Clockwise rotation reveals the complete thin marginal stroke beside the long proof. It is a gently bowed continuous line, with no arrowhead, hatch, or words crossing it except the descender of cf. In original orientation its upper end lies near (215,145) and lower end near (229,1730). I reproduce it as a graphical curved rule, not a cancellation of all adjacent text. The note on a simplifié, cf plus b./h. is present alongside it; clipped main-column fragments at the crop edge are excluded.
